reuse.why: The actions share category selection and reuse budget infrastructure, but fixed-tag detection reimplements the existing extractTagsFromText abstraction.

duplication.why: Repeated category queries are consolidated, although tag recognition is duplicated and the new action repeats the income eligibility guard.

placement.why: Budget eligibility belongs in the budget action layer and registration follows existing conventions, but generic tag parsing belongs in the shared tags module.

scope.why: The diff stays focused on month-wide eligibility, the new spending action, its registration, and related tests.

maintainability.why: Centralized exclusions make subsequent changes straightforward, but a separate tag grammar and caller-owned income filtering leave avoidable policy drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: actions.ts: FIXED_GROUP_TAG and getFixedGroupIds bypass extractTagsFromText in packages/loot-core/src/shared/tags.ts.

disguised_duplication.where: FIXED_GROUP_TAG reshapes shared note-tag recognition into a dedicated regular expression instead of using extractTagsFromText.

abstraction_drift.where: getMonthActionCategories gains the requested includeHiddenCategories parameter and conditional hidden filter; all six month-wide actions use it, although income eligibility remains outside the helper.
